source.locator: Section 5.2.3, pp. 226--227, especially equation (5.27) and the paragraph titled ``Lagrange dual of LP''.
source.verbatim_statement: ``strong duality holds provided the following weaker condition holds''; ``the affine inequalities do not need to hold with strict inequality''; ``dual optimal value is attained''.

attestation.note: Transcribed from pp. 226--227 of Stephen Boyd and Lieven Vandenberghe, Convex Optimization, Cambridge University Press, 2004, in the official author-hosted book PDF.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Adds the finite-dimensional strong-duality leaf used by the proof to the proposition's declared dependency spine.

proposed.statement: Fix \(\delta\in[0,1]\). If \(\mathcal P_\delta(b,q,\omega)=\varnothing\), the audit returns fiber infeasibility and does not certify \(\text{ass:reference-risk-positivity}\). If \(\mathcal P_\delta(b,q,\omega)\neq\varnothing\), that restriction holds if and only if the linear program \(\min\{d_{21,\omega}^{\top}x:E_\omega x=d(b,q),\ F_\delta x\leq0,\ x\geq0\}\) has value at least \(\epsilon\). Equivalently, there are \(\eta\) and \(\kappa\geq0\) satisfying \(E_\omega^{\top}\eta-F_\delta^{\top}\kappa\leq d_{21,\omega}\) and \(d(b,q)^{\top}\eta\geq\epsilon\).
proposed.justification: This implementation audit separates incompatible observed margins from a genuinely nonempty fiber whose late vaccine reference risk is uniformly positive.
proposed.gap: This is an LP audit device for the optional denominator restriction, not a root identification contribution.
proposed.consumer: Software can stop on an infeasible fiber and issue a primal value and dual certificate only after compatibility has been established.
